statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119371 is a stack exhaustion in SQLite's selectExpander(): common table expressions are not counted against SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH, so SQL or a view in an untrusted database file that chains tens of thousands of CTEs recurses without bound and crashes the process. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.54.0: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/bugs/info/2026-10-04T04:58:58Z. The fix is trunk check-in https://sqlite.org/src/info/f54730871303e655, mirrored as https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/e6ff280c839fdfc7418fd5add12e8f32702a17fb, which counts each CTE expansion in resolveFromTermToCte() in src/select.c against the subquery nesting limit; it has no counterpart on the 3.53 maintenance branch. DHI's 3.53.4-r1 build is SQLite 3.53.4 with a backport of that check-in. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. We unpacked the sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static and sqlite-dev packages of every one of those builds on both architectures, each checked against its index checksum. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. sqlite-dev holds only headers, a pkg-config file and the libsqlite3.so link. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1, 3.51.2, 3.53.4 and 3.53.4 in those builds. The 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 builds are built from the upstream 3.51.1, 3.51.2 and 3.53.4 releases, none of which contains the fix. We ran the test with the sqlite3 shell, and with a test program linked once against the shared library and once against the static archive, for every build on x86_64 and aarch64. A query chaining 1,500 common table expressions returns a row in 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 and fails with "VIEWs and/or subqueries nested too deep" in 3.53.4-r1, on both architectures and in all three copies. The x86_64 runs used Docker Desktop's amd64 emulation. So 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 are affected and 3.53.4-r1 is fixed.
